export default "---\ntitle: 'Why Do I Write?'\ndate: '2026-07-06'\nauthor: 'Resul Çalışkan'\ndescription: 'This blog does not exist to post tech news; it exists to document how I think, how I research, and how an idea turns into a product.'\n---\n\nInformation on the internet is more abundant than ever.\n\nThere are hundreds of articles, thousands of videos, and millions of lines of open-source code for almost any technology.\n\nYet, as time passed, I realized something:\n\n> What is truly missing is not information, but **ways of thinking**.\n\nWhen playing a game, everyone sees the same graphics. But some people ask *\"Why is this mechanic engaging?\"*\n\nWhen using an app, most people only notice the feature. I ask *\"Why was it designed this way?\"*\n\nWhen looking at an open-source project, before diving into the code, I try to grasp the core philosophy behind it.\n\nThis blog exists partly for that reason.\n\nRather than content like \"How to use this React hook?\" or \"Which framework is best?\", I want to share how I analyze a problem, the questions I ask, and how an idea matures over time.\n\nBecause in my view, great software engineering starts with asking the right questions before writing a single line of code.\n\n## What will I write about?\n\nThis blog will not revolve around a single narrow topic.\n\nAnything I am curious about, research, or spend time contemplating can find a spot here.\n\nFor instance:\n\n- Game design and player psychology\n- Software architecture & patterns\n- Product development workflows\n- Open-source projects\n- Research methodologies\n- Note-taking systems\n- Artificial Intelligence tools\n- Failed experiments\n- Insights gained from books\n- Daily engineering logs\n\nSometimes a single line from a book...\n\nSometimes a small idea discovered on GitHub...\n\nAnd sometimes a question that has been lingering in my mind for days can be the catalyst for a new post.\n\n## It doesn't have to be perfect\n\nI used to wait for ideas to be fully complete before sharing them.\n\nThen I realized that approach severely slowed down my growth.\n\nThat's why this blog won't be a polished showcase of perfect ideas.\n\nIt will be more like a living workspace.\n\nSome posts won't contain definitive answers.\n\nIn some, my perspective will evolve over time.\n\nAnd some will simply leave behind a great question.\n\nAnd to me, that is the beauty of learning.\n\n## Notes to my future self\n\nIn truth, the primary reader of this blog will be me.\n\nYears from now, when I look back, I want to see not just the projects I built, but how I thought while building them.\n\n> Code gets forgotten over time. But great questions remain.\n\nPerhaps these notes will help someone else walking down a similar path.\n\nEven if they don't, it will remain a living archive of my thoughts.\n\nWelcome.\n";
